article.headline: Beauden Barrett Captains New Zealand Side Boasting 783 Total Test Caps
article.summary: New Zealand faces Wales at Principality Stadium this Saturday in the Nations Championship with Beauden Barrett leading the team for the first time.
article.body: Beauden Barrett will captain the All Blacks for the first time in his 149th Test match when the team squares off against Wales in Cardiff. The veteran side features a combined experience of 783 caps, with head coach Dave Rennie making ten changes to the match-day 23 that faced Scotland last weekend. Anton Segner and Fehi Fineanganofo are set to earn their first Test starts in the round five encounter at Principality Stadium. The selection follows a week of internal review where the coaching staff identified Wales flanker Jac Morgan as a key breakdown threat that must be neutralized to avoid defensive stress. With New Zealand currently holding a 73-year winning streak against their Welsh opponents, the team remains focused on maintaining its dominant record in the Nations Championship. Rennie noted that his familiarity with the Welsh coaching staff, including former colleagues Steve Tandy and Peter Murchie, provides further insight into the tactical adjustments Wales has implemented over the past year. Rennie specifically highlighted Wales' line-out strength and the kicking capabilities of scrum-half Tomos Williams as major factors his team must contain throughout the match. By shuffling the lineup, the coaching staff aims to balance squad depth with the intensity required to respect the opposition's challenge. The match is scheduled for 2:10 PM local time on Saturday. Fans can follow the action live on Sky Sport or access highlights through the official All Blacks digital platforms.

article.headline: Nathan Collins returns to lead Ireland against Austria in Nations League clash
article.summary: Captain Nathan Collins and two other defenders return to the starting line-up for Ireland's UEFA Nations League match against Austria on November 14th.
article.body:
Captain Nathan Collins makes his return to the pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena after missing four consecutive fixtures due to a calf injury. Alongside him, defenders Dara O'Shea and James Abankwah are back in the starting side, bolstering a team that aims to secure a win in Linz to push for promotion to League A. Ireland enters the match with the knowledge that two victories in their final group games—against Austria and Kosovo—will guarantee them the top spot in the group.

Securing this win is critical for Ireland's ambitions. Head coach Heimir Hallgrímsson notes that while finishing in the top two is a primary goal, the team is focused on winning the group outright. A victory would serve as a major step toward promotion, a feat that would mark a significant achievement for the squad. The team is also mindful of disciplinary status, as five players, including Jayson Molumby and Liam Scales, are currently carrying yellow cards and risk suspension for the upcoming decider against Kosovo.

According to RTE.ie, Hallgrímsson has confirmed that Finn Azaz will operate in a deeper midfield role alongside Jayson Molumby. Jack Moylan and Adam Idah are tasked with supporting centre-forward Troy Parrott. On the other side, Austria has made four changes to their team, with Bayern Munich's Konrad Laimer set to captain the side. Austria's squad includes new additions such as Christoph Baumgartner and Philipp Lienhart, as they aim to build on their previous 2-2 draw at the Aviva Stadium.

Following the match in Linz, Ireland will return to Dublin to face Kosovo on Tuesday. Hallgrímsson remains focused on maintaining defensive solidity to avoid repeating the errors seen in the second half of their previous meeting with Austria.

article.headline: FAA Lifts Nationwide Ground Stop After 3,800 Saturday Flights Are Cancelled
article.summary: The FAA ended a five-hour nationwide ground stop on Friday after a telecommunications outage involving legacy system routers disrupted thousands of flights.
article.body: A staggering 3,800 flights remained grounded across the United States on Saturday morning, leaving passengers stranded as the aviation industry struggled to recover from a nationwide shutdown. While the federal airspace is now operating normally, the ripple effects from the five-hour ground stop continue to paralyze major travel hubs, with Delta Air Lines, United, and American reporting hundreds of cancellations each. The crisis began when an aging air traffic control system, described by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy as "incredibly old," buckled under the weight of new security patches. Officials revealed that the trouble originated from Cisco 600 series routers manufactured between 2001 and 2006, which became overloaded with data and provided inconsistent information, forcing a total system reboot. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin confirmed the outage was caused by these technical failures, noting there was no indication of any nefarious act during the disruption. For travelers, the immediate future remains uncertain as airlines work to reposition crews and clear a backlog of thousands of delays. Secretary Duffy warned that passengers should anticipate continued disruptions as carriers scramble to reschedule flights into early next week. Major airports, including Hartsfield-Jackson in Atlanta, Chicago O'Hare, and New York's John F. Kennedy, have borne the brunt of the chaos. Flight tracking data from FlightAware and Flightradar24 indicates the total impact reached approximately 10,000 flights impacted during the initial grounding period. While safety protocols are being strictly maintained, the scale of the fallout underscores the fragility of the nation's legacy aviation infrastructure. Officials are currently monitoring the system closely to prevent a recurrence of the technical failure.

article.headline: البرتغال تُواجه الدنمارك في دوري الأمم بدون كريستيانو رونالدو اليوم
article.summary: يخوض المنتخب البرتغالي مواجهة مرتقبة ضد نظيره الدنماركي ضمن منافسات الجولة الخامسة من دوري الأمم الأوروبية في غياب كريستيانو رونالدو.
article.body:
تتجه أنظار عشاق كرة القدم إلى المواجهة التي تجمع بين المنتخب البرتغالي ونظيره الدنماركي ضمن فعاليات الجولة الخامسة من بطولة دوري الأمم الأوروبية. وتدخل البرتغال هذا اللقاء في ظروف استثنائية، حيث أكدت التقارير الصادرة عن موقع Sports Mole أن الفريق سيخوض المباراة مفتقداً لجهود نجمه الأبرز كريستيانو رونالدو، مما يضع الجهاز الفني واللاعبين أمام تحدٍ جديد لتعويض غياب القائد والمؤثر الهجومي في صفوف المنتخب.

تكمن أهمية المباراة للقارئ والمتابع في التوقعات الهجومية العالية؛ حيث يبرز المنتخب البرتغالي كأحد أخطر الفرق في البطولة الحالية، بمتوسط تسجيل يصل إلى 2.25 هدف في المباراة الواحدة، مع فارق أهداف إيجابي يبلغ +5. هذه الأرقام تجعل من المباراة ساحة محتملة لغزارة تهديفية، وهو ما يتابعه المحللون في Sports Betting Dime عبر ترجيح تجاوز حاجز الـ 3.5 أهداف في اللقاء.

من الناحية التاريخية، يمتلك المنتخب البرتغالي سجلاً قوياً ضد الدنمارك، إذ تمكن من تحقيق الفوز في ثلاث من أصل أربع مواجهات سابقة جمعت بين الطرفين. ومن بين تلك النتائج، يبرز انتصار البرتغال بنتيجة 4-2 الذي تحقق في الأول من أكتوبر 2026. وتستعد البرتغال للدخول في هذه المباراة معتمدة على أسلوبها الذي يركز على الهجمات المرتدة السريعة التي أثبتت فعاليتها خلال مباريات البطولة الأربع الماضية.

تأتي هذه المباراة ضمن سلسلة من المواجهات القوية في الجولة الخامسة من دوري الأمم الأوروبية، والتي تشهد تداخل حسابات التأهل والهروب من الهبوط. وبينما تحاول البرتغال تأكيد تفوقها التاريخي والاستمرار في تقديم أدائها الهجومي القوي، تسعى الدنمارك لتقديم أداء تنافسي يقلب الموازين في الميدان رغم صعوبة الاختبار أمام الأداء البرتغالي المتوازن في البطولة.

news.og_title: Portugal Changes How No. 7 Is Written to Honor Cristiano Ronaldo
news.og_desc: The Portugal football team is making a change to how the No. 7 is written to honor the recently-retired Cristiano Ronaldo. Ronaldo, who wore the number and went on to make it his own as “CR7,” retired from international soccer last week, ending a remarkable career that spanned six World Cups, a European title, and the men’s all-time international scoring record. “Time to debut a new 7.
